entities.summary: Raffaele "Raf" Vallone was an Italian actor and footballer. One of the top male Italian stars of the 1950s and 1960s, he first became known for his association with the neorealist movement, and found success in several international productions. On stage, he was closely associated with the works of Arthur Miller. He played the role of Eddie Carbone in A View from the Bridge several times, including Sidney Lumet's 1962 film adaptation, for which he won the David di Donatello for Best Actor. Raf Vallone was a journalists & chroniclers from Tropea (1916-02-17, Tropea–2002-10-31). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Raf Vallone was a prominent Italian actor and footballer who played key roles in neorealist productions and Arthur Miller's works. His performance in A View from the Bridge earned him a David di Donatello award, contributing to his lasting legacy as a leading figure in mid-20th-century Italian cinema.
